## A — Exam authority — Utah Class D knowledge preparation

Issuer is the Utah Department of Public Safety Driver License Division [A02].
Preparation follows the current Utah Driver Handbook edition shown on the cover material [A03].
The verified passing threshold for the written knowledge check is eighty percent, scored as 80 [A01].
Question count, question bank size, test format, and time limit are not stated on the assigned handbook pages (verify).
Edition effective date is not stated as a single handbook date on the assigned pages (verify).
Handbook facts used in this dossier come from the official issuer handbook snapshot tier [A02].

sections.heading: B — Audience & Scope
sections.markdown:
## B — Audience & Scope
First-time applicants preparing for regular passenger-car written knowledge in Utah, studying in English from the current handbook.
Content level is plain everyday language with driving terms explained when first used.
Prerequisite assumption is never-licensed status with no prior road experience required.

sections.heading: C - Alcohol, drugs and driving
sections.markdown:
## C - Alcohol, drugs and driving (Section 10)
Coverage: printed pages 51-55 [A01]. Pedagogic emphasis only.

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Alcohol weakens judgment that draws on stored experience for new problems [A01].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Vision is the main driving sense and is harmed at 0.02 BAC for each driver [A01].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A80
A single alcoholic drink can already impair the ability to drive a motor vehicle [A80].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Harm starts with the first drink, so the safest choice is not to drive after use [A01].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
Illegal, store-bought, and prescribed drugs plus strong emotions can impair driving [A01].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A02
Under age 21 it is unlawful to buy, hold, or drink alcohol under zero tolerance [A02].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A02
Ages 13 through 20 face license loss of one year then two years for alcohol acts [A02].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A81
A driver younger than twenty-one who has measurable alcohol in the body faces denial of driving privileges for six months on the first offense. A repeat offense within ten years of an earlier denial brings a loss lasting two years or through the twenty-first birthday, with the longer period controlling [A81].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A82
Over 0.05 BAC breaks the law, and 0.04 does so for CDL holders in Utah [A82].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A82 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A83
Refusal of the chemical test selected by the officer brings license revocation: eighteen months for a first offense, then thirty-six months for repeat offenses. For someone younger than twenty-one, the first revocation lasts two years or through the twenty-first birthday, whichever lasts longer. A repeat revocation for that younger driver lasts thirty-six months or through that birthday, again using the longer period [A83].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A83 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A04
A first DUI brings an 18-month car device term, or three years if under 21 at arrest [A04].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A05
A court-called interdicted person gives up the card and pays a 7.00 admin fee [A05].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0065]

High yield ranked: limits and Not-a-Drop first, refusal and device terms next.
Misconceptions: one drink is safe; under-limit means lawful; refusal has no cost.
Mnemonics: JVC-R for judgment vision color reaction effects.
Glossary: BAC; implied consent; Not-a-Drop; alcohol-restricted; interlock.

sections.heading: C2 — KG handoff hints — Alcohol/Drugs & Driving (Section 10)
sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG handoff hints — Alcohol/Drugs & Driving (Section 10)

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
Impairment of driving judgment, vision, color perception, and reaction speed begins with the first drink, so waiting to feel visibly drunk is not a safe standard [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint impairment-effects; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec10-R02.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
Vision used for driving is affected at a very low alcohol level, while a single drink can already degrade vehicle control even before obvious intoxication appears [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint impairment-effects; prereq_hint sec10-R01; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-R01, sec10-R03.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A01
Strong feelings such as anger, worry, excitement, fear, or sadness can distract thinking and degrade driving, and should be resolved by cooling off, allowing extra trip time, or letting another person drive [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint emotions-vs-substances; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec10-R01.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A02
A driver age 21 or older violates the alcohol law above the stated general operating threshold, with a lower threshold for commercial operation, and can also violate by being unsafe below those numbers [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint bac-limits; prereq_hint sec10-R01; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-R02, sec10-R07.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A02
A person aged 13 through 20 convicted of possessing alcohol, consuming alcohol, or entering a bar while underage faces a court-ordered license suspension that lengthens on a repeat offense, with timing anchored to conviction or to the 16th birthday for the youngest drivers [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint under-21-penalties; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-R06.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A02
A driver under 21 with any measurable alcohol in the body faces denial of driving privileges for months on a first occurrence and for years or until age 21 on a repeat within a decade, even if no license has yet been issued [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint under-21-penalties; prereq_hint sec10-R05; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-R05, sec10-R08.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A02
A first driving-under-influence conviction at 21 or older suspends the license for months, while a second or later conviction suspends it for years, with administrative suspension authority beginning weeks after arrest [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint dui-suspension; prereq_hint sec10-R04; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-R06, sec10-R08.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A03
Driving or operating a motorboat implies agreement to breath, blood, urine, or oral-fluid testing when a peace officer requests it, and refusing causes a longer revocation that grows on repeat offenses, with a special until-age-21 rule for younger drivers [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint implied-consent; prereq_hint sec10-R04; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-R06, sec10-R07.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A03
After an alcohol-related action, a driver carries an alcohol-restricted status for a multi-year tier or for life depending on offense count and type, and driving with any measurable alcohol during that period revokes the license for a year [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint restricted-status; prereq_hint sec10-R07; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-R10, sec10-R11.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A04
A first driving-under-influence conviction brings an ignition-interlock-only driving period measured in months, longer when the driver was under 21 at arrest, while a second or later covered violation or a test-refusal revocation brings a multi-year interlock period [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint interlock-periods; prereq_hint sec10-R09; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-R09, sec10-R11.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A04
An interlock-restricted driver must have the device checked at least about every two months, and each missed check or attempt to start with measurable alcohol adds about two more months to the requirement [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint interlock-compliance; prereq_hint sec10-R10; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-R09, sec10-R10.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A05
A court-designated interdicted person surrenders the license or card and pays a small administrative fee to add interdicted status, while a voluntary applicant completes an agreement form without that fee and must keep the status for at least about a month [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint interdicted-status; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-R05.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0065]
